DESCRIPTION:Speaker(s): #RAC #Learning #ImpactWe warmly invite you to an inspiring dinner hosted by Rotaract Club Zurich International\, where we are pleased to welcome our guest speaker\, Paolo Rodi. This session will explore high-altitude illnesses from both a medical and public health perspective\, with a focus on the real risks faced by climbers and trekkers worldwide—especially in remote areas where access to care is limited.The talk will include insights from a recent expedition in Argentina\, where a lightweight CPAP-based approach was tested as a potential tool for managing altitude-related conditions in the field. This will serve as a practical example of how innovation can be adapted to extreme environments.The discussion will also examine the Nepalese context\, highlighting the working conditions of guides and porters\, as well as the social and cultural dynamics of mountain tourism. Particular attention will be given to unequal exposure to risk and the broader implications for safety and sustainability in high-altitude regions.Speaker Bio Paolo Rodi Is a medical doctor with a background in trauma and emergency surgery\, currently working in Switzerland. His work focuses on disaster medicine\, global surgery\, and humanitarian health\, with a particular interest in improving access to care in resource-limited settings.He is actively involved in mountain and extreme environment medicine\, combining clinical practice\, research\, and field experience in high-altitude regions such as the Andes and the Himalayas. He is also co-founder of Medical Pirates\, a project aimed at making medical knowledge more accessible through engaging and educational content.We look forward to sharing an evening of insight\, meaningful conversation\, and inspiration with you.General InfoThe event will take place at Blaue Ente\, located at Kulturareal Mühle Tiefenbrunnen\, Seefeldstrasse 223.We will meet at 7:00 PM\, and the presentation will start at 7:20 PM (30 minutes) followed by dinner.The cost for the main course and a soft drink will be CHF 45–50\, depending on the selected menu.Do not miss it! ✨

DESCRIPTION:Speaker(s): We warmly invite you to an inspiring evening hosted by Rotaract Club Zurich International\, where we are delighted to welcome our guest of honour\, Roberto Bilton.

Drawing from his experience at the world’s largest brewer\, our speaker will share his perspectives on global sourcing and the craft of negotiation\, exploring how Anheuser-Busch InBev secures the ingredients behind some of the world’s most beloved beers\, and what it takes to strike deals that span continents\, currencies\, and cultures.  Speaker Bio

Roberto Bilton is a dynamic sourcing and procurement leader based in Switzerland. As Global Sourcing Manager for Adjuncts EMEA at Anheuser-Busch InBev\, he steers the sourcing strategy behind iconic names such as Budweiser\, Corona\, Stella Artois\, and Leffe\, negotiating with suppliers across Europe\, the Middle East\, and Africa from his base in Zug as part of the company’s Global Procurement Office.

His journey spans three continents. Beginning his career in management consulting in São Paulo\, he went on to serve as Chief Operating Officer at CarBraxx\, part of Grupo SHC\, and to lead projects at the Fundação Lemann\, one of Brazil’s most respected foundations\, before pursuing a full-time STEM MBA in Management Science at the prestigious University of Virginia Darden School of Business\, where he was honoured with the Darden School Foundation Scholarship. He also holds a degree in Business Administration from Insper. A former competitive athlete\, Roberto channels the drive to set new records into every negotiation\, pairing sharp strategic instinct with a relentless focus on results.

At eight years old, Natasha became a young carer, balancing school and growing up while caring for her mother, often feeling misunderstood and alone. That experience shaped her education, her career, and ultimately her mission. When she learned that 180’000 young carers in Switzerland remain unseen, she founded Caring4YoungCarers to break the silence and make sure every young carer is visible, acknowledged and supported.

Young carers are children, teenagers and young adults aged 5 to 25 who look after a family member with a chronic illness, addiction or disability. They make up 10% of Swiss youth, roughly one to three students in every classroom. Most of them do not know that they are young carers, and do not know that support exists.

Natasha will share her personal story and the work behind Caring4YoungCarers: the information and support network for young carers themselves, the educational workshops that help teachers, healthcare staff and social workers recognise hidden caring roles, and the growing partnership network with organisations such as the Swiss Red Cross Canton Zurich, Stand By You Schweiz, EnableMe and Global Shapers Zurich.

An evening about visibility, empathy and practical support, followed by open discussion over dinner.

General Info

The event takes place at Blaue Ente, in the Kulturareal Mühle Tiefenbrunnen at Seefeldstrasse 223. We meet at 19:00. The keynote starts at 19:15, followed by dinner.

The main course with a soft drink costs around CHF 50.

Rotaract Club Zurich International is delighted to welcome Karim Mustaghni for an interactive keynote on Exponential Thinking in the Age of AI.

Most leaders are wired to think linearly, using the past to predict what comes next. But when technology, markets, and expectations change exponentially, the past stops being a reliable guide. What is needed instead is the willingness to imagine, question, experiment, and adapt.

Karim will take us through the building blocks of exponential thinking and make the case that  curiosity may be the single most important skill for navigating an exponential world. He combines the uniquely human strengths of curiosity, creativity, and collaboration with what he calls Human-AI Thinking: using AI as a thinking partner rather than a thinking replacement. Expect a session on how to meet change and uncertainty and turn both into a source of innovation. Come with questions.

Speaker Bio

Karim Mustaghni is a founder, lecturer, and speaker who helps leaders and teams develop Exponential Thinking in the age of AI, enabling them to anticipate disruption, adapt faster, and turn emerging technologies into new opportunities. With more than 15 years of global experience across six continents, he is CEO of The Creativs, an artist, and co-founding investor at Chefslist, the market-leading AI backbone of food wholesale in the DACH region, connecting over 10,000 businesses with their food suppliers. He lectures at the EBS Executive School and has delivered more than 250 keynotes and interactive executive sessions worldwide. The former community director at Sigma Squared Society has been recognised as a World Economic Forum Global Shaper and a BMW Foundation Responsible Leader.

General Info

The event takes place at Blaue Ente, in the Kulturareal Mühle Tiefenbrunnen at Seefeldstrasse 223. We meet at 19:00. The keynote starts at 19:15, followed by dinner.

The main course with a soft drink costs around CHF 50.

We are delighted to welcome Alec McShane of Palantir Technologies as Guest of Honour at out December dinner & talk at Blaue Ente. 

Alec leads Palantir's commercial business across Europe from the company's office in Zurich. His focus is on the relationship  with private-sector clients, the companies that bring Palantir's software into their production lines, supply chains and daily decisions. 

Alec works at the front line between one of the most important technology companies in the world and some of the most demanding institutions in Europe. Few people are better placed to explain how that trust is built, on client at a time. 

Alec will speak about these three themes: 

What makes Palantir unique, technically and culturally.
The go-to-market approach in a market as conservative as ours. 
Sovereignty in the broader sense. Why geopolitical alliances hold less firmly than they once did, and what the world actually means now.
An evening filled with technology, trust and power, followed by questions and dinner.

Places are limited.

As the year draws to a close, Rotaract Club Zürich International, warmly invites you to its Christmas dinner, high above the city, at Chalet

Züriberg.

Picture a wooden chalet on the Züriberg. A fire in the heart, candlelight on every table, and the lights of Zürich spread out below. It is the perfect place to raise a glass to everything this year has brought us: the guests of honour who joined us at our dinner, the hours spent volunteering with Essen für Alle, and the friendships that began over a good meal and even better conversation. 

Members, partners, friends and first-time guests are welcome. If someone in your life has been curious about the club, this is the evening to bring them. 

The Venue

Chalet

Züriberg

opens its doors only for the winter season. Set on the edge of the forest next to the Sorell Hotel

Zürichberg, it looks out over the city, the lake and, on a clear night, the Alps. The house is known for its fondue by the fireplace, which makes it the ideal table for a long, festive evening together. 

General Info

We meet at Chale

Züriberg

at 8:15pm, with dinner to follow. The chalet sits up on the hill, so dress warmly for the short walk in.
